interest: Militarization of Japanese education and the end of academic freedom in the 1930s.
overview: U.S. State Department decimal file 894.42 (covering 1930 to 1939) documents Japanese educational administration, textbook revision, expanding youth militarization, and the suppression of academic freedom in schools and universities during the pre-World War II decade. Composed of diplomatic despatches, cross-reference sheets, consular reports, and military attaché intelligence reports, the file details early-decade legislative debates over state subsidies for compulsory education and short-lived plans in 1931 to moderate martial narratives in elementary textbooks. Following the Manchurian Incident, the documentation charts a swift turn toward militant nationalism, including Chinese diplomatic reporting on anti-foreign and expansionist indoctrination in Japanese textbooks, the 1935 consolidation of youth continuation schools into the Young People's School (Seinen Gakkō) system to provide nationwide pre-conscription military drill to over 1.7 million students, incidents at Christian institutions like Doshisha University, and the 1938–1939 state campaign led by Education Ministers Marquis Kōichi Kido and General Sadao Araki to dismantle faculty election autonomy and purge liberal scholars at Tokyo Imperial University.

subfiles.about: State Department cross-reference note and attached report extract concerning Ministry of Education plans to revise national textbooks to emphasize social history over military stories.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1671 Transmitting Report and Pamphlet on Anti-Foreign Japanese Textbooks
